english.title: Deal with funds / economic resources owned / held / controlled by a designated person - Ukraine
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without authority of a licence granted by the Treasury, dealt with funds or economic resources belonging to, owned, held or controlled by a designated person, namely **(..SPECIFY DETAILS of DESIGNATED PERSON..), knowing or having reasonable cause to suspect that you were dealing with such funds or economic resources
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 3(1), 10(1) and 12(1) of the Ukraine (European Union Financial Sanctions) (No.2) Regulations 2014.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

economic resources belonging to / owned / held / controlled by
a designated person
circumventing / contravention of regulation 3(1)
knowing / having reasonable cause to suspect
that they were dealing with funds / economic resources in such a manner

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 3(1) outlines the meaning of deal with for the purpose of the offence.
(ii) A designated person means any person, entity or body listed in Annex I to the Council Regulation.
(iii) Regulation 14 states that consent of the Attorney General is needed to bring proceedings for this offence, except for summary offences.
(iv) For provisions regarding the laying of proceedings, see regulation 13 for full detail of how proceedings may be brought in the relevant jurisdiction.
(v) The offence does not apply to anything done under the authority of a licence granted by the Treasury. If a licence is revoked by the Treasury, the offence may still be made out as per regulation 9.
(vi) This offence may be committed by conduct wholly or partly outside the United Kingdom when it is conduct of a UK national or a body incorporated or constituted under the law of the United Kingdom.

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 7 years imprisonment and/or fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Note
In relation to an offence committed before section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 comes in to force, the reference to 12 months imprisonment in relation to summary offences, above, is to be read as reference to 6 months imprisonment.
